subject: URGENT: Reserved capacity queue collapse - immediate mitigation & next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah@orbitalai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@orbitalai.com
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Reserved pool: sudden queue collapse impacting production

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a major degradation on our reserved pool (pool-id: rsv-us-east-7) at ~08:08 UTC. Tail latency jumped from ~120ms to 2-3s and many requests returned 5xx or timed out. Our ingestion pipeline has partial outages. This is customer-impacting across multiple regions that route to the reserved capacity.

What we observed: 
- Spike in queue length on dedicated nodes, sustained for ~12m
- Rapid evictions and increased retry traffic
- 504s in the frontend with trace ids attached

We attached a short trace screenshot and a small replay of recent request IDs (customer-replay-requests.txt) to help debugging. Please advise immediate mitigation steps and ETA for a fix. Our SRE is on standby in case you need access.

Thanks,
Sarah
Ops Lead, Orbital AI

Attachments: orbital-trace-snippet-20250514.png (image), customer-replay-requests.txt (text)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@orbitalai.com>, ops+infra@orbitalai.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 08:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Reserved pool: sudden queue collapse impacting production

Hi Sarah — thank you for the quick heads up and the artifacts. We've escalated to our on-call infra lead (Karthik) and the account team (Ben, Marissa). Initial acknowledgement and next steps below: 

Immediate actions (in progress):
1) Route a subset of OrbitalAI traffic to a warm standby in us-east while we stabilize the pool (expected < 15m).
2) Gather allocator and eviction logs from the affected nodes (we requested allocator-dump-20250514.tar.gz and a short timeline).
3) Apply temporary concurrency-cap increase and throttle retry backoff to reduce amplification.

Can you confirm you are OK with the traffic diversion to the warm standby? Also please share any VIPs / IPs we should avoid during the switchover. We will follow up with a post-incident call and a proposed remediation timeline.

— Stephanie
Principal Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sarah Park <sarah@orbitalai.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 08:42:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Reserved pool: sudden queue collapse impacting production — technical update

Quick technical summary and immediate mitigation we applied: 

What happened (high level):
- A controller-side miscount in live-concurrency after a recent autoscaler adjustment caused the allocator to mark multiple warm nodes as cold simultaneously for pool rsv-us-east-7. That triggered large-scale prefix eviction and an unexpected single-cycle rebalance. Evictions + client retries created a feedback loop that pushed queue length up and frontend latencies over SLOs.

Actions taken (08:30–08:40 UTC):
- Rolled out an immediate controller patch to correct the concurrency counter (hotfix INF-4721).
- Increased per-tenant concurrency floor for OrbitalAI to prevent premature cold-marking.
- Manually bound OrbitalAI to two warm standby nodes to flatten eviction churn.
- Disabled aggressive retry amplification in the gateway for 30 minutes.

Current status: queues are dropping and latency is trending back toward baseline; we are monitoring for error flares. Full allocator dumps have been gathered (allocator-dump-20250514.tar.gz) and uploaded to our internal evidence bucket.

Next steps:
- Produce a reproducible replay with your provided request IDs (Sarah) to validate the fix.
- Prepare a postmortem with timeline, root cause and remediation (ETA for draft: 48 hours).
- Propose permanent guardrails (controller counter validation, autoscaler safety net).

I'll keep this thread updated as we validate.

— Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: allocator-dump-20250514.tar.gz (logs), patch-diff-INF-4721.patch (text)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Reserved pool: sudden queue collapse impacting production — customer plan and credits

Sarah — quick note to capture the customer-facing action plan and our commitments: 

1) Immediate: Traffic diversion to warm standby completed with your OK (confirmed). Error rate and tail latency are improving; we will keep the diversion in place until monitoring shows stability for 2h.
2) Short-term (48h): Full postmortem draft (timeline + RCA + patch details) delivered to you within 48 hours. That will include the allocator dumps and the patch we applied (INF-4721).
3) Medium-term (2–4 weeks): Controller validation tests and an autoscaler safety net to prevent re-entrance into the eviction loop.
4) Compensation: We will issue a service credit equivalent to 6 hours of dedicated capacity for the affected window; account team (Ben) will follow up on procurement next steps if you need manual billing adjustments.

We propose a 30-minute postmortem sync: Thu May 15, 2025 16:00 UTC (let me know if another time works). Please confirm the following so we can proceed: 
- Permission to re-run the recorded replay against a dev harness for validation
- Acceptance of traffic diversion to the warm standby (already in flight unless you object)

Thanks again for raising this quickly — we’ll deliver the evidence packet and the draft postmortem by Fri EOD.

— Stephanie
Principal Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
